Announcing Loom — A versatile framework for multi-modal verification of effectful computations in Lean

image.png

We’re thrilled to release Loom, a new framework for reasoning about effectful monadic programs in Lean.
Loom provides a unified foundation for verifying, testing, and executing effectful programs — bringing together ideas from monadic semantics, SMT-based automation, and Lean’s native proof infrastructure.

Key Features

  • Multi-modal verification
    Loom’s metatheory is designed to support diverse verification styles. You can seamlessly set up verification semantics for your monadic programs — proving both the absence and presence of bugs, reasoning about exceptions, and more.
    Thanks to Lean’s executable monads, you can also run and fuzz-test your programs under the same semantics used for verification.

  • Intrinsic proof style
    Verification in Loom follows a Dafny- and Verus-like approach: annotate your monadic Lean code with pre-/post-conditions and loop invariants, and Loom’s SMT-based automation will discharge as many obligations as possible.
    When automation falls short, you can seamlessly continue the proof interactively using Lean’s tactics.

  • Advanced reasoning about termination
    Loom integrates with Lean’s new partial_fixpoint mechanism, enabling reasoning about partial correctness. It also lets you separately verify functional correctness (programs don’t go wrong) and termination (programs eventually complete).

  • Monad transformer for non-determinism
    Loom ships with a universal monad transformer for non-determinism. Computations in this monad support non-deterministic choice, can be executed under sound verification semantics, and are ideal for reasoning about textbook algorithms and competitive programming problems.

  • Full access to Lean’s ecosystem
    As a Lean library, Loom inherits the entire Lean ecosystem, including mathlib. Our examples feature verified implementations of sparse matrix operations built directly on top of mathlib’s algebraic foundations.

Beyond Loom: Velvet and Veil

Built on top Loom, we developed:

  • Velvet — a Dafny-like verifier for imperative programs in Lean, and
  • Veil 2.0 — a re-engineered version of Veil verifier for distributed protocols, now with sound symbolic model checking and executable semantics.

Relation to mpl

Loom complements mpl, an alternative framework by @Sebastian Graf and the LeanFRO team, which focuses on extrinsic reasoning about monadic Lean code.
While Loom emphasizes intrinsic verification, we’re excited to explore collaborations toward a unified framework serving all Lean users.

Resources

  • Source code: github.com/verse-lab/loom
  • POPL ’26 paper (conditionally accepted): verse-lab.github.io/papers/loom-preprint.pdf
